claude.sample_unit: AI-generated patient-friendly radiology reports (graded by 80 lay participants in field testing)

links.outcome: Interrater agreement of rubric grades among lay and radiologist raters against reference-standard grades
links.effect: Lay and radiologist research-team members had almost-perfect intergroup agreement (α=0.87); additional radiologists had substantial (α=0.65) and lay participants moderate (α=0.51) interreader agreement.
links.quote: Lay and radiologist research-team members (n=3 participants each; 60 reports) had almost-perfect intergroup agreement (α=0.87) for overall grade assignments.

links.outcome: Agreement of raters and AI with reference grades on patient-friendly report clarity, certainty, tone, and content
links.effect: Lay participants (480 reports) had moderate agreement (κ=0.43) with reference-standard grades; AI had moderate agreement (κ=0.44); rule-based distribution decisions using AI grades agreed 88.1% with reference-based decisions.
links.quote: Across 480 reports, AI had moderate agreement (κ=0.44) with prespecified reference-standard grades; rule-based distribution decisions using AI-assigned grades had 88.1% agreement with rule-based distribution decisions using reference-standard grades.

unlisted_practices: Rubric-based quality assurance gate (including AI grader) before releasing AI-generated patient-friendly radiology reports

links.outcome: Overall grade agreement between lay and radiologist raters
links.effect: n=3 each; 60 reports; α=0.87 for overall grade assignments.
links.quote: Lay and radiologist research-team members (n=3 participants each; 60 reports) had almost-perfect intergroup agreement (α=0.87) for overall grade assignments.

links.effect: Lay/radiologist readers had α=0.51/0.65 and 91.2%/95.8% agreement between subjective and rubric rule-based distribution decisions.
links.quote: Additional lay (n=19) and radiologist (n=12) participants, each evaluating six reports, had moderate (α=0.51) and substantial (α=0.65) interreader agreement, respectively, for overall grade assignments and 91.2% and 95.8% agreement, respectively, between subjective and rubric rule-based distribution decisions.

links.outcome: AI rubric agreement with reference standards
links.effect: Across 480 reports, κ=0.44 with reference-standard grades; rule-based decisions had 88.1% agreement with reference-standard decisions.
links.quote: Across 480 reports, AI had moderate agreement (κ=0.44) with prespecified reference-standard grades; rule-based distribution decisions using AI-assigned grades had 88.1% agreement with rule-based distribution decisions using reference-standard grades.

unlisted_practices: Using ChatGPT-5 to apply a quality and safety rubric to AI-generated patient-friendly radiology reports

links.outcome: Interreader and distribution-decision agreement for patient-friendly report quality rubric
links.effect: Lay and radiologist evaluators achieved moderate (α=0.51) and substantial (α=0.65) agreement for overall grades, and 91.2% and 95.8% agreement between subjective and rubric rule-based distribution decisions.
links.quote: Additional lay (n=19) and radiologist (n=12) participants, each evaluating six reports, had moderate (α=0.51) and substantial (α=0.65) interreader agreement, respectively, for overall grade assignments and 91.2% and 95.8% agreement, respectively, between subjective and rubric rule-based distribution decisions.

screen.practice: rubric-based quality review of AI-generated patient-friendly reports before release
screen.reason: The study develops and tests a standardized quality assessment rubric and decision rule (withholding unsafe reports) as a safeguard to ensure the safety and clarity of AI-generated patient-friendly radiology reports before distribution.

primary.practice: quality assessment rubric and automated safety withholding rule
